issues.claim: Azure SignalR Service configured with `ServerStickyMode` set to `Required`
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt of host-and-deploy/server does not show this wording. I know it from the same page: its Azure SignalR Service section sets `ServerStickyMode` to `Required` (`options.ServerStickyMode = ServerStickyMode.Required`). The fact is correct. The Azure Container Apps session affinity and Data Protection claims are shown in the excerpt.

issues.claim: In .NET 10 you can persist selected component state so that a new circuit restores it
issues.problem: This is correct for .NET 10, which added circuit state persistence and declarative persistent state. The excerpts do not show it, but the text names no API and is worded generally.
issues.suggestedFix: No change needed. Optionally add a link to the Blazor state management docs.

issues.claim: Razor components can be hosted inside a JavaScript app as root components or custom elements
issues.problem: The fetched js-spa-frameworks excerpt says the custom elements feature (Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.CustomElements) is "currently experimental, unsupported, and subject to change or be removed at any time". The Angular/React component generation is also experimental. The answer offers this as a coexistence path in a long-term-risk decision with no caveat. A candidate would learn that it is a stable, supported option.
issues.suggestedFix: Qualify it in both locales. For example: "Razor components can be registered as root components for JavaScript (supported since .NET 7); exposing them as custom elements is experimental and unsupported, so do not rely on it for a multi-year plan."

issues.problem: The item shows the fetch status as 'unknown', not 'ok' as the rebuttal states. The excerpt is an older, non-latest version of the page, but it still supports the cited claims (shared .NET logic, C# productivity, static rendering without a large JS bundle). Acceptable, but the rebuttal misreports the status.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep the link. No content change is needed.

issues.claim: a major version every November, an LTS version every two years
issues.problem: The support policy excerpt shows .NET 8 and .NET 10 as LTS and .NET 11 as STS, with a release every November. The sentence about the cadence is cut off in the excerpt, so the "LTS every two years" statement is only indirectly supported.
issues.suggestedFix: Keep it. Optionally soften it to "a major release every November; LTS and STS releases alternate".
